gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a '100 W from any port' charger can still drop the laptop below 65 W once a phone is plugged in: techtest.org measured the 3-port Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 splitting 45 W + 45 W on C1 + C2, so how many watts a charger gives one device on its own says nothing about what the laptop keeps with two devices plugged in.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT got. The cited service.anker.com A2688 page gives Anker's full table (65+35, 65+22.5, and 12+12 on C2+USB-A), so the advice to use the right port is already covered for Anker. cadiens.com gives UGREEN 4-port at 65+30 and warns that C3 cannot replace C2. soldermag.com, computingforgeeks.com and thisusb.com/guides/best-usb-c-chargers list 65+35 / 65+30 / 70+30 splits. None of them names the Baseus AH22 or any 100 W charger that splits 45+45, and none lists a charger that keeps 65 W on both ports (AOHi Youth 140W). computingforgeeks says outright that it found no 100 W charger described as 45+45.
decides: It confirms that the picks have to come from the maker's two-device table and not from single-port watts. It removes the Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22, one of our listed products and a candidate in the cluster map, from the 65 W line on the C1 + C2 pair techtest gives (techtest prints no C1+C3 or C2+C3 split). The Anker Prime 100W A2688 (65+35, C1 only) and UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-Port (65+30, C1+C2 only) stay as the top rows. AOHi The Youth 140W, also one of ours, joins the line as the only charger here where Notebookcheck says both ports hold 65 W, so the phone and laptop can go into either port. That claim comes from a launch article, not a test, so it should not be ranked above the maker-tabled picks without a measured split.

findings.source_title: Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 im Test: 100W USB-C-Ladegerät mit Display und AVS (Michael Barton, techtest.org, 2026-11-23)
findings.note: Michael Barton (techtest.org) gives 'USB-C 1 + 2 = 45 W + 45 W'. Any single port gives 100 W alone. Barton also found it held 100 W for about 40 minutes before dropping to 80 W. Gentle Mode caps each port at 20 W. AVS 9–20 V/5 A (tested with iPhone 18 Pro Max), PPS 5–20 V/5 A on all USB-C ports. techtest prints no C1+C3 or C2+C3 split.

findings.note: Notebookcheck: when two devices charge at once, 'both drop to the 65W standard'. This is a launch article quoting the maker, not a measurement. Unlike the Anker and the UGREEN 4-port, which port the laptop goes into does not matter here.
